We would be grateful if you could consider for publication our manuscript entitled “*Estimating censored demand in family planning supply chains: forecast accuracy, inventory implications, and public health outcomes*” as an Original Research article in *Production and Operations Management*.

Accurate demand estimation is critical for ensuring contraceptive availability, yet frequent stockouts and service interruptions systematically censor observed consumption and bias forecasts—perpetuating cycles of under-stocking and unmet need. Existing forecasting methods often ignore or uniformly treat censorship, limiting their operational relevance for inventory decisions in low-resource settings.

In this manuscript we introduce the Truncated Conformal Kalman Filter (TCKF), a novel framework that integrates a Tobit-style Kalman Filter with conformal prediction. TCKF (i) explicitly distinguishes partial censorship (stockouts) from full censorship (interruptions/no-stock-received), (ii) adapts process noise to prolonged uncertainty, and (iii) produces distribution-free predictive intervals and sample paths that are directly usable in inventory simulation. We evaluate TCKF on realistic synthetic experiments and LMIS data from the family planning program in Côte d’Ivoire, assessing point and probabilistic accuracy and downstream inventory and public-health outcomes (Inventory Value Added, product availability, service level).

Our results show that treating censored observations appropriately improves forecast accuracy, yields better calibrated uncertainty estimates, and materially improves inventory performance and public-health impact compared with standard benchmarks. The approach is practical, generalizable, and directly targets the decision problems faced by supply-chain planners in humanitarian and public-health settings.

We believe that our research makes a significant contribution to the field by addressing a critical challenge and providing actionable insights for improving demand forecasting in low-resource settings.

Thank you very much for considering this manuscript. We look forward to the opportunity to contribute to your esteemed journal and to hearing from you in due course.
